conceptual assets.information: Instruction words returned by the instruction bus, including compressed-format information and decompressed instructions, which the CPU depends on for execution. The stream enters through the instruction response data and leaves through the frontend instruction and format outputs.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The instruction stream can be exposed at frontend_o.instr and frontend_o.compr on lines 225-246 and 268-269. Changing the response data or the logic producing the instruction outputs can change the fetched instruction on lines 137-138 and 225-246. Fetch state, buffer capacity and valid-generation logic can withhold instruction delivery through lines 124, 145, 224, 229, 239, 244 and 267. The privilege and debug qualifiers on the outgoing fetch request can cause an integration-level mode to select a different response and produce an incorrect instruction through lines 129-130.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could observe the instruction output, alter returned instruction data, or manipulate fetch qualifiers and flow control to execute incorrect code or prevent instruction delivery.

conceptual assets.concept: Instruction fetch address and program counter
conceptual assets.information: The current program counter and next instruction-fetch address select which instruction is requested from the instruction bus. CPU execution depends on this state progressing to the intended instruction locations.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The current fetch address can reveal control flow through ibus_req_o.addr on line 123. Changing ctrl_i.pc_nxt or the registered and incremented fetch.pc changes the requested address on lines 102-114. A corrupted address can prevent the required instruction transfer or send execution to an unusable location through the fetch request at line 123.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could observe fetch addresses or overwrite the next program counter so that execution follows an unintended path or instruction fetching stops.

conceptual assets.information: The privilege mode associated with the current instruction fetch is captured and attached to the outgoing bus request. The memory system depends on it to apply the intended access permissions.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The privilege mode is observable in the outgoing ibus_req_o.priv field on line 129. An altered ctrl_i.cpu_priv value changes the stored fetch privilege on line 115 and therefore the request qualifier.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could observe the privilege level or replace it with another mode, causing an instruction access to receive inappropriate permissions or be rejected.

conceptual assets.information: The processor debug indication qualifies instruction-bus requests and can cause the memory-side fetch to be treated as a debug access. Normal fetch behavior depends on this qualifier being correct.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Changing ctrl_i.cpu_debug changes the debug qualifier presented on ibus_req_o.debug at line 130, which can alter the handling of the instruction request.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could assert or clear the debug qualifier so that a normal instruction fetch is handled as the wrong kind of access.

conceptual assets.information: The bus error indication associated with a fetched word is carried into the prefetch data and returned as the frontend fault status. The CPU depends on this status to distinguish a valid fetch from a failed one.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Changing ibus_rsp_i.err or the fault-generation logic can suppress a real fetch error or inject a false one at frontend_o.fault through lines 137-138 and 220, 235 and 270.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could modify the bus error bit or fault output so that the CPU executes after a failed fetch or unnecessarily treats a valid fetch as an error.

conceptual assets.information: The request strobe and frontend delivery-status signals control whether an instruction transfer is initiated and accepted. The frontend and CPU require these signals to make progress through the instruction stream.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Changing the generated strobe, valid indication or halt indication can cause the receiving bus or CPU to interpret the transfer incorrectly through lines 124, 145, 224, 229, 239, 244 and 267. The same signals can withhold or block instruction progress when they suppress a request or report that delivery is unavailable on those lines.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could suppress fetch requests, falsely deassert instruction validity, or falsely assert the halted status to stop normal instruction delivery.

conceptual assets.information: The fence qualifier requests the instruction-bus side to apply the requested instruction-fetch ordering behavior. Correct instruction visibility and ordering depend on this command being preserved.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: An altered ctrl_i.if_fence value directly changes the outgoing fence command on line 134 and can change the ordering behavior applied to instruction fetching.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could suppress or inject the fence qualifier so that instruction fetches observe an unintended ordering or stale instruction contents.
